summary.title: Reflections on 10,000 Hours of Programming
summary.one_liner: A personal list of 31 hard-won lessons on pure coding craft, from preferring existing code and deleting code to managing dependencies, configuration, and abstractions.
keywords: easy to use hard to misuse api
configuration progression environment variables cli flags
read source code instead of stackoverflow
takeaways: Read the source code of the tools you use; it is often faster than searching for answers online.
Delete code aggressively, avoid syntactic sugar, and treat ugly code and comments that are not docstrings as signs of a design problem.
Be careful with dependencies: avoid taking direct dependencies on tiny libraries you could rewrite, and on large libraries that should have been small.
Understand how your program runs in production and in its build pipeline, since that is part of understanding the program.
Good APIs are easy to use and hard to misuse; configuration tends to evolve from hardcoded values through several layers and back.
summary.summary: The author, a former Google and Kubernetes engineer, shares 31 reflections on pure coding craft drawn from about 15 years of programming, explicitly excluding career and people-management advice. The lessons are short, opinionated bullet points covering tooling, code simplicity, dependencies, comments, API design, configuration, and abstraction layers. The page is a personal essay rather than a tutorial, so the points are assertions from experience with brief justifications rather than step-by-step guidance. It notes that most points apply to experienced programmers rather than beginners.
